exposure: Conservative approach to hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (hsPDA) (precise fluid restriction and judicious use of diuretics)
Previous approach to hsPDA (higher rates of primary PDA ligation and less conservative fluid restriction)
cohort: The study included 348 very low birthweight infants (VLBWIs) diagnosed with hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (hsPDA) across two distinct treatment periods.
finding: A conservative approach to hsPDA, involving more precise fluid restriction and judicious use of diuretics, led to better clinical outcomes and improved cognitive scores at 18-24 months corrected age compared to a period with more active PDA ligation.
